### Importing Peaks ###
```{r peaks}
threshold     <- 260  # Peaks over threshold (m3/s), change for initial threshold
steps_per_day <- 96   # 15-minute data resolution (24 * 4)

# Put Pitnacree on a continuous 15-minute grid
pit <- tibble(
  Timestamp = seq(
    min(pitnacree$Timestamp, na.rm= TRUE),
    max(pitnacree$Timestamp, na.rm=TRUE),
    by = "15 min"
  )
) %>%
  left_join(
    pitnacree %>% dplyr::select(Timestamp, Value),
    by = "Timestamp"
  )

flow <- pit$Value
flow_noNA <- replace_na(flow, 0) # 0 ensures peak detection ignores missing intervals


# Extract candidate peaks exceeding the specified threshold
raw <- findpeaks(flow_noNA, minpeakheight = threshold, minpeakdistance = 1, zero = "0")

cand <- tibble(
  max_flow   = raw[, 1],
  max_time   = raw[, 2],
  peak_begin = raw[, 3],
  peak_end   = raw[, 4]
) %>%
  arrange(max_time) %>%
  mutate(ttr = max_time - peak_begin) # Time to rise in 15-min steps


# Compute average time to peak from "clean" isolated events
near_other <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(cand)), function(i) {
  any(abs(cand$max_time[-i] - cand$max_time[i]) < 7 * steps_per_day)
})

clean <- cand %>%
  mutate(clean = flow[peak_begin] < 0.5 * max_flow & !near_other & !is.na(flow[peak_begin]))

avg_ttr <- mean(clean$ttr[clean$clean])
min_sep <- 3 * avg_ttr
cat(sprintf("Avg time to peak: %.2f hours | Min FEH separation: %.2f hours\n", avg_ttr / 4, min_sep / 4))


# Filter candidate peaks using FEH independence criteria 
keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(cand))
last <- 1

for (k in 2:nrow(cand)) {
  sep <- cand$max_time[k] - cand$max_time[last]
  independent <- sep >= min_sep
  
  if (independent) {
    trough <- min(flow[cand$max_time[last]:cand$max_time[k]], na.rm = TRUE)
    independent <- trough < (2/3) * cand$max_flow[last]
  }
  
  if (independent) {
    last <- k
  } else if (cand$max_flow[k] > cand$max_flow[last]) {
    keep[last] <- FALSE
    last <- k
  } else {
    keep[k] <- FALSE
  }
}

peaks_passed <- cand[keep, ]
n_years <- sum(!is.na(flow)) / (steps_per_day * 365.25)
```

```{r find peaks UPDATED}
threshold     <- 260  # Peaks over threshold (m3/s), change for initial threshold
steps_per_day <- 96   # 15-minute data resolution (24 * 4)

# Put Pitnacree on a continuous 15-minute grid
pit <- tibble(
  Timestamp = seq(
    min(pitnacree$Timestamp, na.rm= TRUE),
    max(pitnacree$Timestamp, na.rm=TRUE),
    by = "15 min"
  )
) %>%
  left_join(
    pitnacree %>% dplyr::select(Timestamp, Value),
    by = "Timestamp"
  )

flow <- pit$Value
flow_noNA <- replace_na(flow, 0) # 0 ensures peak detection ignores missing intervals


# Extract candidate peaks exceeding the specified threshold
# CHANGED: peakpat allows a flat top (repeated values at the peak); the default
# pattern skips any peak whose maximum value repeats.
raw <- findpeaks(flow_noNA, minpeakheight = threshold,
                 peakpat = "[+]{1,}[0]*[-]{1,}")

cand <- tibble(
  max_flow   = raw[, 1],
  max_time   = raw[, 2]
) %>%
  arrange(max_time)

# CHANGED: robust start of rise. findpeaks' own start point is reset by any
# small dip or flat step on the rising limb. Instead, start of rise = last time
# in the 5 days before the peak when flow was within 10% (of the rise) of the
# lowest flow in that window.
lookback <- 5 * steps_per_day
rise_tol <- 0.10

cand$peak_begin <- sapply(cand$max_time, function(tp) {
  w0   <- max(1, tp - lookback)
  seg  <- flow[w0:tp]
  base <- min(seg, na.rm = TRUE)
  w0 - 1 + max(which(seg <= base + rise_tol * (flow[tp] - base)))
})

cand <- cand %>%
  mutate(ttr = max_time - peak_begin) # Time to rise in 15-min steps


# Compute average time to peak from "clean" isolated events
# CHANGED: isolation is judged against one peak per flood (the largest within
# +/- 3 days), so a flood's own small wiggles don't make it look "non-isolated".
dominant <- sapply(cand$max_time, function(tp) {
  w <- max(1, tp - 3 * steps_per_day):min(length(flow), tp + 3 * steps_per_day)
  flow[tp] >= max(flow[w], na.rm = TRUE)
})
dom_times <- cand$max_time[dominant]

near_other <- sapply(cand$max_time, function(tp) {
  any(abs(dom_times - tp) < 7 * steps_per_day & dom_times != tp)
})

clean <- cand %>%
  mutate(clean = dominant & flow[peak_begin] < 0.5 * max_flow & !near_other &
                 !is.na(flow[peak_begin]) &
                 peak_begin > max_time - lookback)  # CHANGED: rise start not at window edge

avg_ttr <- mean(clean$ttr[clean$clean])
min_sep <- 3 * avg_ttr
cat(sprintf("Clean events: %d | Avg time to peak: %.2f hours | Min FEH separation: %.2f hours\n",
            sum(clean$clean), avg_ttr / 4, min_sep / 4))


# Filter candidate peaks using FEH independence criteria (unchanged)
keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(cand))
last <- 1

for (k in seq_len(nrow(cand))[-1]) {
  sep <- cand$max_time[k] - cand$max_time[last]
  independent <- sep >= min_sep

  if (independent) {
    trough <- min(flow[cand$max_time[last]:cand$max_time[k]], na.rm = TRUE)
    independent <- trough < (2/3) * cand$max_flow[last]
  }

  if (independent) {
    last <- k
  } else if (cand$max_flow[k] > cand$max_flow[last]) {
    keep[last] <- FALSE
    last <- k
  } else {
    keep[k] <- FALSE
  }
}

peaks_passed <- cand[keep, ]
n_years <- sum(!is.na(flow)) / (steps_per_day * 365.25)


# ---- NEW: hydrograph extraction for part 2 ---------------------------------
# Fixed window either side of each peak, aligned at the peak (offset 0).
# Events whose window runs off the record or contains missing data are dropped.
hydro_halfw <- 3 * steps_per_day   # +/- 10 days; set to match your part 2 window
thin        <- 1                    # keep every 4th point (hourly); 1 = all 15-min points

offsets <- seq(-hydro_halfw, hydro_halfw, by = thin)

peaks_passed <- peaks_passed %>%
  mutate(
    Timestamp      = pit$Timestamp[max_time],
    ttr_hours      = ttr / 4,
    # Duration = hours of the continuous stretch around the peak with flow
    # above half the peak (a neighbouring flood can't inflate it)
    halfwidth_hours = sapply(max_time, function(tp) {
      below <- which(flow < 0.5 * flow[tp])
      start <- max(c(0, below[below < tp])) + 1
      end   <- min(c(length(flow) + 1, below[below > tp])) - 1
      (end - start + 1) / 4
    }),
    # Window lies within the record and has no missing data
    complete_window = max_time - hydro_halfw >= 1 &
                      max_time + hydro_halfw <= length(flow) &
                      sapply(max_time, function(tp) {
                        w <- max(1, tp - hydro_halfw):min(length(flow), tp + hydro_halfw)
                        !anyNA(flow[w])
                      }),
    # No larger flood inside the window (otherwise the normalised shape
    # exceeds 1 away from the peak and mixes two events)
    peak_is_window_max = sapply(max_time, function(tp) {
      w <- max(1, tp - hydro_halfw):min(length(flow), tp + hydro_halfw)
      max(flow[w], na.rm = TRUE) <= flow[tp]
    })
  )

events_p2 <- peaks_passed %>% filter(complete_window, peak_is_window_max)

# Hydrograph matrix: one row per event, one column per time offset
Q_raw <- t(sapply(events_p2$max_time, function(tp) flow[tp + offsets]))   # m3/s
Y_shape     <- Q_raw / events_p2$max_flow                                       # normalised: peak = 1
t_days <- offsets / steps_per_day                                         # time from peak (days)

cat(sprintf(paste0("Independent events: %d over %.1f years\n",
                   "Dropped for part 2: %d incomplete window, %d larger flood within +/-%g days\n",
                   "Hydrographs for part 2: %d\n"),
            nrow(peaks_passed), n_years,
            sum(!peaks_passed$complete_window),
            sum(peaks_passed$complete_window & !peaks_passed$peak_is_window_max),
            hydro_halfw / steps_per_day, nrow(events_p2)))

```

## Emma D


```{r scale peaks to same grid, show what each coefficient represents}
# Uses Y, t_days and events_p2 from the peaks chunk.
# Y: n x K matrix of hydrographs normalised so the peak = 1, aligned at the
# peak (t_days = 0), on a fixed +/-3-day window.

Yt <- t(Y_shape)                                    # K x n: one column per event, as before
pk <- events_p2$max_flow                      # peak flows (part 1 / emulator input)

rmse <- function(A, B) sqrt(colMeans((A - B)^2))   # per-event RMSE (normalised scale)

# ---- Method 1a: one global orthogonal polynomial over the whole window -------

fit_global <- function(deg) {
  B   <- poly(t_days, deg)
  fit <- lm(Yt ~ B)
  list(coefs = t(coef(fit)), Hhat = fitted(fit))
}

degs <- 1:20
deg_table <- data.frame(
  deg          = degs,
  n_coefs      = degs + 1,
  median_rmse  = sapply(degs, function(d) median(rmse(Yt, fit_global(d)$Hhat))),
  median_peak  = sapply(degs, function(d) median(fit_global(d)$Hhat[t_days == 0, ])),
  pct_negative = sapply(degs, function(d) 100 * mean(fit_global(d)$Hhat < 0))
)
print(round(deg_table, 3))

deg <- 4                                   # from the table
g   <- fit_global(deg)
B_global <- cbind(1, poly(t_days, deg))    # the design matrix lm() used

C <- g$coefs
colnames(C) <- c("intercept", paste0("poly_", 1:deg))

rebuild <- function(Bm) B_global %*% t(matrix(Bm, ncol = ncol(C)))   # S x p -> K x S

max(abs(rebuild(C) - g$Hhat))              # should be ~0: rebuild reproduces the fits

mu  <- colMeans(C)
sdv <- apply(C, 2, sd)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
for (j in 2:4) {
  lo <- mu; lo[j] <- mu[j] - 2 * sdv[j]
  hi <- mu; hi[j] <- mu[j] + 2 * sdv[j]
  matplot(t_days, cbind(rebuild(mu), rebuild(lo), rebuild(hi)), type = "l",
          lty = c(1, 2, 2), col = c("black", "blue", "red"),
          xlab = "Days from peak", ylab = "Flow / peak flow",
          main = paste(colnames(C)[j], ": mean ± 2 SD"))
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```


```{r diagnostics for MVN}
# ---- Diagnostics for the shape coefficients --------------------------------
logQ <- log(events_p2$max_flow)
n <- nrow(C); p <- ncol(C)
cat(sprintf("n = %d events, p = %d coefficients, full MVN has %d parameters\n",
            n, p, p + p * (p + 1) / 2))

# 1. Pairs plot, points coloured by peak size (dark = larger flood)
cols <- gray(1 - rank(logQ) / (n + 1))
pairs(C, pch = 21, bg = cols, cex = 1.2,
      main = "Shape coefficients (darker = larger peak)")

# 2. Marginal QQ plots, one per coefficient, with Shapiro-Wilk p-value
par(mfrow = c(2, ceiling(p / 2)))
for (j in 1:p) {
  qqnorm(C[, j], main = sprintf("%s  (SW p = %.2f)", colnames(C)[j],
                                shapiro.test(C[, j])$p.value))
  qqline(C[, j])
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# 3. Joint normality: squared Mahalanobis distances vs chi-squared quantiles
d2 <- mahalanobis(C, colMeans(C), cov(C))
qq <- qqplot(qchisq(ppoints(n), df = p), sort(d2),
             xlab = bquote(chi[.(p)]^2 ~ "quantiles"),
             ylab = "Squared Mahalanobis distance",
             main = "Multivariate normality check")
abline(0, 1)


# 4. Correlations between coefficients (does dependence matter?)
print(round(cor(C), 2))

# 5. Does shape depend on flood size? Spearman correlation with log peak
dep <- t(sapply(1:p, function(j) {
  ct <- cor.test(C[, j], logQ, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
  c(rho = unname(ct$estimate), p_value = ct$p.value)
}))
rownames(dep) <- colnames(C)
print(round(dep, 3))

```

```{r MVN simulation, spaghetti plots}
library(mvtnorm)
set.seed(2026)

# ---- Fit the MVN to all events ------------------------------------------------
mu    <- colMeans(C)
Sigma <- cov(C)

# ---- Simulate shapes ------------------------------------------------------------
S     <- 1000
C_sim <- rmvnorm(S, mu, Sigma)          # S x p simulated coefficient vectors
Y_sim <- rebuild(C_sim)                 # K x S simulated normalised hydrographs

# Reference: the observed curves' own polynomial fits (same smoothness as simulations)
Y_fit <- rebuild(C)                     # K x n

# ---- 1. Observed vs simulated spaghetti plots -----------------------------------
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
ylims <- range(Y_shape, Y_fit, Y_sim[, 1:100])
matplot(t_days, t(Y_shape), type = "l", lty = 1, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15),
        ylim = ylims, main = "Observed", xlab = "Days from peak", ylab = "Flow / peak flow")
matplot(t_days, Y_fit, type = "l", lty = 1, col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.15),
        ylim = ylims, main = "Polynomial fits to observed", xlab = "Days from peak", ylab = "")
matplot(t_days, Y_sim[, 1:100], type = "l", lty = 1, col = rgb(1, 0, 0, 0.15),
        ylim = ylims, main = "Simulated (100 of 1000)", xlab = "Days from peak", ylab = "")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# ---- 2. Do the simulated bands match the fitted bands? ------------------------
band <- function(Y) apply(Y, 1, quantile, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))   # Y is K x m
b_fit <- band(Y_fit); b_sim <- band(Y_sim)
matplot(t_days, t(b_fit), type = "l", lty = c(2, 1, 2), col = "blue", lwd = 2,
        xlab = "Days from peak", ylab = "Flow / peak flow",
        main = "Median and 90% bands: fitted observed (blue) vs simulated (red)")
matlines(t_days, t(b_sim), lty = c(2, 1, 2), col = "red", lwd = 2)

# ---- 3. Plausibility of simulated hydrographs --------------------------------
at_peak   <- Y_sim[t_days == 0, ]
max_where <- t_days[apply(Y_sim, 2, which.max)]
plaus <- c(
  `% with any negative flow`           = 100 * mean(apply(Y_sim, 2, min) < 0),
  `% whose maximum is not at t = 0`    = 100 * mean(abs(max_where) > 0.25),  # > 6 h away
  `% exceeding 1 anywhere`             = 100 * mean(apply(Y_sim, 2, max) > 1),
  `median value at t = 0`              = median(at_peak)
)
round(plaus, 2)

# ---- 4. Hydrological features: simulated vs fitted observed -------------------
dt <- diff(t_days)[1]
feat_of <- function(Y) data.frame(volume    = colSums(Y) * dt,
                                  halfwidth = colSums(Y >= 0.5 * apply(Y, 2, max)) * dt)
f_fit <- feat_of(Y_fit); f_sim <- feat_of(Y_sim)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
for (v in names(f_fit)) {
  qqplot(f_fit[[v]], f_sim[[v]], xlab = "Fitted observed", ylab = "Simulated",
         main = v, pch = 19, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.4))
  abline(0, 1)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

## Harry


```{r harry}
# 1. Hydrograph matrix: one row per event, hourly values from 72h before to 72h after the peak,
#    divided by the peak flow so each row is a shape
pk_idx <- sort(peaks_passed$max_time)
get_window <- function(i) {
  lo <- i - 72 * 4;  hi <- i + 72 * 4
  if (lo < 1 || hi > length(flow)) return(NULL)
  seg <- flow[lo:hi]
  if (mean(is.na(seg)) > 0.05) return(NULL)
  seg <- approx(seq_along(seg), seg, xout = seq_along(seg), rule = 2)$y
  seg[seq(1, length(seg), by = 4)] / seg[289]
}
segs <- lapply(pk_idx, get_window)
Y <- do.call(rbind, segs[!sapply(segs, is.null)])
t_h <- -72:72
dim(Y)

# 2. PCA (centre, don't scale: all columns already on the same scale)
pca_result <- prcomp(Y, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)

# 3. Variance explained
plot(pca_result)
head(cumsum(pca_result$sdev^2) / sum(pca_result$sdev^2), 10)

# 4. Loadings as a function of time
plot(t_h, pca_result$rotation[, 1], type = "l", col = "red", ylim = range(pca_result$rotation[, 1:2]),
     xlab = "Hours from peak", ylab = "Loading", main = "Loadings for PC1 and PC2")
lines(t_h, pca_result$rotation[, 2], col = "blue")
legend("bottomright", legend = c("PC1", "PC2"), col = c("red", "blue"), lty = 1)

# 5. Scores
head(pca_result$x[, 1:3])

# 6. Reconstruct hydrograph 1 using k PCs
mean_hydro <- colMeans(Y)
k <- 3
recon <- mean_hydro + pca_result$x[1, 1:k] %*% t(pca_result$rotation[, 1:k])
plot(t_h, Y[1, ], type = "l", lwd = 2, xlab = "Hours from peak", ylab = "Q / Qmax",
     main = "Original vs PCA reconstruction (hydrograph 1)")
lines(t_h, recon, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("Original", "Recon"), col = c("black", "red"), lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 2)
```

### 7. SETTINGS AND SHARED OBJECTS  (change tuning choices here only)

```{r harry_settings}

cfg <- list(k_pc = 8,        # number of parameters (PCs) kept; 8 = 95% of variance here
            use_log = TRUE,  # TRUE = model log(shape): keeps simulated flows positive (recommended)
            m_sim = 100,     # simulated hydrographs per held-out event in cross-validation
            n_boot = 200,    # bootstrap resamples for the PCA stability check
            seed = 1)
set.seed(cfg$seed)

# fig(): draws to the screen AND saves a PNG into ./plots (300 dpi) for Overleaf
fig <- function(name, w, h, code) {
  code <- substitute(code);  dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
  eval(code, parent.frame())
  png(file.path("plots", paste0(name, ".png")), width = w, height = h, units = "in", res = 300)
  eval(code, parent.frame());  dev.off()
}

keep_ev   <- !sapply(segs, is.null)             # events that survived get_window()
Qpeak     <- flow[pk_idx[keep_ev]]              # peak flow of each row of Y (m3/s)
peak_time <- pit$Timestamp[pk_idx[keep_ev]]
n_ev <- nrow(Y);  nt <- ncol(Y);  ctr <- which(t_h == 0)
stopifnot(length(Qpeak) == n_ev, all(abs(Y[, ctr] - 1) < 1e-8))
cat("Events:", n_ev, "| grid points:", nt, "| peak range:", round(range(Qpeak)), "m3/s\n")

# Shape features used for EDA and validation (same 'time to peak' idea as part 1)
shape_features <- function(s) {
  lo <- which(s[1:(ctr - 1)] < 0.5);  hi <- which(s[(ctr + 1):length(s)] < 0.5)
  l <- if (length(lo)) max(lo) else NA
  r <- if (length(hi)) ctr + min(hi) else NA
  c(volume = sum(s),        # area under the shape (hours at peak flow)
    rise_h = ctr - l,       # hours from last point below 50% of peak to the peak
    width_h = r - l)        # hours spent above 50% of the peak
}
```

### 9. A GENERIC REPRESENTATION:  x_i(t) ~= mu(t) + sum_j z_ij A_j(t)

```{r harry_representation}
#    type = "pca"  : mu = mean shape, A = principal-component loadings
#    type = "poly" : mu = 0, A = orthogonal polynomial basis (so the same code scores Emma's method)

fit_rep <- function(X, type = c("pca", "poly"), p) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  if (type == "pca") {
    pc <- prcomp(X, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
    mu <- pc$center;  A <- pc$rotation[, 1:p, drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    mu <- rep(0, ncol(X))
    A  <- if (p == 1) matrix(1, ncol(X), 1) else cbind(1, poly(seq_len(ncol(X)), p - 1))
  }
  Z <- (sweep(X, 2, mu) %*% A) %*% solve(crossprod(A))   # least-squares parameters for each event
  list(mu = mu, A = A, Z = Z)
}
to_scale   <- function(Y) if (cfg$use_log) log(Y) else Y
from_scale <- function(X) if (cfg$use_log) exp(X) else X

#Choose the number of parameters: leave-one-event-out reconstruction error
loo_recon <- function(type, p_grid) {
  X <- to_scale(Y)
  sapply(p_grid, function(p) {
    sq <- sapply(seq_len(n_ev), function(i) {
      rp <- fit_rep(X[-i, , drop = FALSE], type, p)
      z  <- (X[i, ] - rp$mu) %*% rp$A %*% solve(crossprod(rp$A))   # project the held-out event
      mean((Y[i, ] - from_scale(rp$mu + as.numeric(rp$A %*% t(z))))^2)
    })
    sqrt(mean(sq))
  })
}
p_grid  <- 1:12
rec_tab <- data.frame(p = p_grid, PCA = loo_recon("pca", p_grid), Polynomial = loo_recon("poly", p_grid))
pca_s   <- prcomp(to_scale(Y), center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)   # PCA on the modelling scale (log if use_log)
cum_pve <- cumsum(pca_s$sdev^2) / sum(pca_s$sdev^2)
cat("\nLeave-one-out reconstruction RMSE (Q/Qpeak) at the same number of parameters\n"); print(round(rec_tab, 4))
cat("PCs for 90% / 95% of variance:", which(cum_pve >= .9)[1], "/", which(cum_pve >= .95)[1],
    "| chosen k_pc =", cfg$k_pc, "\n")

fig("fig2_choose_k", 9, 4.2, {
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(1:15, cum_pve[1:15], type = "b", pch = 19, ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "Number of PCs",
     ylab = "Cumulative variance explained", main = "Variance explained")
abline(h = c(.9, .95), lty = 2); abline(v = cfg$k_pc, col = "red", lty = 2)
matplot(rec_tab$p, rec_tab[, 2:3], type = "b", pch = 19, lty = 1, col = c("red", "blue"),
        xlab = "Number of parameters", ylab = "LOO reconstruction RMSE", main = "Representation error")
legend("topright", c("PCA", "Polynomial"), col = c("red", "blue"), pch = 19, lty = 1, bty = "n")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
})

#Full-data fit with the chosen k: what each component does, and are the scores related to peak size?
rp_full <- fit_rep(to_scale(Y), "pca", cfg$k_pc)
Z       <- rp_full$Z
fig("fig3_pc_effects", 11, 4, {
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
for (j in 1:3) {
  eff <- 2 * sd(Z[, j]) * rp_full$A[, j]
  matplot(t_h, from_scale(cbind(rp_full$mu, rp_full$mu + eff, rp_full$mu - eff)), type = "l", lty = c(1, 2, 2),
          col = c("black", "red", "blue"), lwd = 2, xlab = "Hours from peak", ylab = "Q / Qpeak",
          main = sprintf("PC%d: %.0f%% of variance", j, 100 * pca_s$sdev[j]^2 / sum(pca_s$sdev^2)))
  if (j == 1) legend("topright", c("mean shape", "+2 SD", "-2 SD"), col = c("black", "red", "blue"), lty = c(1, 2, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = .8)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
})

dep <- t(sapply(1:cfg$k_pc, function(j) {
  ct <- cor.test(Z[, j], log(Qpeak), method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
  c(PC = j, rho = unname(ct$estimate), p = ct$p.value, shapiro_p = shapiro.test(Z[, j])$p.value)
}))
cat("\nScores vs log(peak flow) (Spearman) and normality of scores (Shapiro-Wilk)\n"); print(round(dep, 3))
fig("fig4_scores_pairs", 7, 7, pairs(Z[, 1:4], col = adjustcolor(pk_col, .8), pch = 19, labels = paste0("PC", 1:4),
      main = "Scores (dark = larger peak)"))

# Stability of the leading PCs: resample events, refit, compare loadings (|correlation| with original)
boot_load <- replicate(cfg$n_boot, {
  pb <- prcomp(to_scale(Y)[sample(n_ev, replace = TRUE), ], center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
  sapply(1:4, function(j) abs(cor(pb$rotation[, j], pca_s$rotation[, j])))
})
cat("\nBootstrap stability of loadings (|correlation| with full-data PC): 5%, 50%, 95%\n")
print(round(apply(boot_load, 1, quantile, c(.05, .5, .95)), 2))
fig("fig5_pc_stability", 6, 4, boxplot(t(boot_load), names = paste0("PC", 1:4), ylim = c(0, 1),
    ylab = "|correlation| with full-data loading", main = "Bootstrap stability of loadings"))
```

### 10. Simulating shapes and validating (leave-one-event-out)

```{r harry_validation}
# rep  : "none" (raw shapes) | "pca" | "poly"
# dist : "fixed" = mean shape, no uncertainty (current SEPA practice) | "mvn" = multivariate normal for the parameters z

fit_model <- function(Ytr, rep, dist, k) {
  if (rep == "none") return(list(rep = rep, dist = dist, mu = colMeans(Ytr)))
  rp <- fit_rep(to_scale(Ytr), rep, k)
  c(rp, list(rep = rep, dist = dist, zbar = colMeans(rp$Z), S = cov(rp$Z)))
}
sim_shapes <- function(m, n) {
  if (m$rep == "none") return(matrix(m$mu, n, length(m$mu), byrow = TRUE))
  z <- if (m$dist == "fixed") matrix(m$zbar, n, length(m$zbar), byrow = TRUE) else MASS::mvrnorm(n, m$zbar, m$S)
  from_scale(sweep(matrix(z, n) %*% t(m$A), 2, m$mu, "+"))
}
clean_shape <- function(raw) { s <- pmax(raw, 0); s[, ctr] <- 1; s }      # no negative flow; s(0) = 1
simulate_hydrographs <- function(n, Qpeak, model) Qpeak * clean_shape(sim_shapes(model, n))   # n x nt flows (m3/s)

# energy score: proper score for a whole curve (lower = better); rewards sharp AND well-calibrated ensembles
es_fun <- function(S, y) {
  m <- nrow(S)
  (mean(sqrt(rowSums(sweep(S, 2, y)^2))) - sum(dist(S)) / (m * (m - 1))) / sqrt(length(y))
}


# 11. LEAVE-ONE-EVENT-OUT CROSS-VALIDATION (same k for PCA and polynomial)

methods <- data.frame(name = c("Fixed mean shape (SEPA)", "PCA + MVN", "Polynomial + MVN"),
                      rep  = c("none", "pca", "poly"), dist = c("fixed", "mvn", "mvn"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_ev), function(i) do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(methods)), function(j) {
  md <- fit_model(Y[-i, , drop = FALSE], methods$rep[j], methods$dist[j], cfg$k_pc)   # refit on n-1 events
  S  <- clean_shape(sim_shapes(md, cfg$m_sim));  y <- Y[i, ]                          # simulate, score vs held-out
  q  <- apply(S[, -ctr], 2, quantile, c(.05, .25, .75, .95));  yy <- y[-ctr]
  data.frame(event = i, method = methods$name[j], rmse_mean = sqrt(mean((colMeans(S) - y)^2)),
             energy = es_fun(S, y), cov50 = mean(yy >= q[2, ] & yy <= q[3, ]), cov90 = mean(yy >= q[1, ] & yy <= q[4, ]))
}))))

ES <- sapply(methods$name, function(m) cv$energy[cv$method == m])
bi <- replicate(1000, sample(n_ev, replace = TRUE))
gain <- t(sapply(methods$name, function(m) quantile(apply(bi, 2, function(ix) mean(ES[ix, m] - ES[ix, 1])), c(.025, .975))))
tab <- aggregate(cbind(rmse_mean, energy, cov50, cov90) ~ method, data = cv, FUN = mean)
tab <- tab[match(methods$name, tab$method), ]
tab$n_param <- c(0, rep(cfg$k_pc + cfg$k_pc * (cfg$k_pc + 1) / 2, 2))
tab$energy_gain_vs_fixed <- tab$energy - tab$energy[1];  tab$CI_low <- gain[, 1];  tab$CI_high <- gain[, 2]
cat("\nLEAVE-ONE-EVENT-OUT VALIDATION (lower = better for RMSE/energy; coverage targets 0.50 / 0.90)\n")
print(format(tab, digits = 3), row.names = FALSE)

#Figure: simulated vs observed shapes (full-data fit, one draw per observed event)
m_pca <- fit_model(Y, "pca", "mvn", cfg$k_pc);  m_fix <- fit_model(Y, "none", "fixed", 0)
sim_pca <- clean_shape(sim_shapes(m_pca, n_ev))
fig("fig6_sim_vs_obs", 11, 4.5, {
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
matplot(t_h, t(Y), type = "l", lty = 1, col = adjustcolor("grey30", .3), ylim = c(0, 1.5),
        main = "Observed shapes", xlab = "Hours from peak", ylab = "Q / Qpeak")
matplot(t_h, t(sim_pca), type = "l", lty = 1, col = adjustcolor("red", .3), ylim = c(0, 1.5),
        main = "PCA simulated shapes", xlab = "Hours from peak", ylab = "Q / Qpeak")
matplot(t_h, cbind(t(apply(Y, 2, quantile, c(.05, .5, .95))), t(apply(sim_pca, 2, quantile, c(.05, .5, .95))), m_fix$mu),
        type = "l", lty = c(2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 1), col = c(rep("black", 3), rep("red", 3), "blue"), lwd = c(1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2),
        ylim = c(0, 1.2), main = "5/50/95% envelopes", xlab = "Hours from peak", ylab = "Q / Qpeak")
legend("topright", c("observed", "PCA simulated", "fixed (SEPA)"), col = c("black", "red", "blue"), lty = 1, bty = "n", cex = .7)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
})

fig("fig7_energy_scores", 6, 4.5, boxplot(ES, names = c("Fixed", "PCA", "Polynomial"), outline = FALSE,
    ylab = "Energy score per held-out event (lower = better)", main = "Leave-one-event-out energy score"))

```

```{r checks4}
# Compare different hydrograph window lengths
window_hours <- c(24, 36, 48, 72)

window_check <- lapply(window_hours, function(h) {

  ratios <- sapply(peaks_passed$max_time, function(i) {

    lo <- i - h * 4
    hi <- i + h * 4

    if (lo < 1 || hi > length(flow)) return(NA_real_)

    seg <- flow[lo:hi]

    if (anyNA(seg)) return(NA_real_)

    max(seg) / flow[i]
  })

  data.frame(
    Window = paste0("±", h, " hours"),
    Usable = sum(!is.na(ratios)),
    Problematic = sum(ratios > 1.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    Percentage = round(100 * mean(ratios > 1.05,
                                  na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  )
})

do.call(rbind, window_check)
```
